scope: Analysis plan fixed before CSV inspection; active CSV is exclusively locked until collector shutdown.
qualification: Collector exit must be0; complete CSV and final stdout/stderr retained; any ETW lost-buffer/lost-event/overflow warning invalidates every resource-independent cadence result.
One warmup plus three measured fresh processes per player/workload; retain every attempted run. A workload with any incomplete or unidentified measured run remains unqualified.
Filter by exact coordinator-owned PID and recorded process lifetime/QPC windows. Reject foreign player processes; never reuse a swapchain address across processes.

For each process, require exactly one chain whose CPUStartQPC submission rate is80..120% of nominal source FPS in the last5s of the40s playback window and last1.5s of confirmed resumed playback, and at most1present/sec in the pause interior after excluding0.5s at each edge. More than one candidate is ambiguous and unqualified.
Require matching guarded1280x720 canvas/DPI, source fixture hash and display source metadata. Actual CPUStartQPC interior is windowStart+5s through+35s; no dropped/undisplayed rows excluded.

Only after identification, compute per-run distributions from finite positive DisplayedTime values in that fixed30s interior; retain NA as undisplayed and report its count/fraction. Also report submission count/rate, presented/displayed counts, median/p95/p99/max duration, and durations>1.5times nominal frame interval.

PresentMon presentation events and displayed durations do not establish unique decoded frames, physical panel timing, audio continuity, equal decoder/filter quality or overall player superiority. No process CPU comparison from these instrumented runs.
protocolLimit: The1200s collector started before coordinator staging. If it ends before a complete workload, retain that workload as partial and repeat a complete independently captured batch; do not splice different sessions or drop the affected run.
metricsSource: DisplayedTime is the per-present display duration in milliseconds, NA when not displayed; CPUStartQPC identifies the event time under --qpc_time.
